checklist.item: Pre-existing tracked defects still open

residual_risks: Rate limiting is unverified where it is actually enforced. redis/token_bucket.lua was read by no lens; bucket atomicity, key expiry, capacity application and the retry-millis behind Retry-After are assumed correct from the Java side. Every new unauthenticated capability names 'there is a bucket' as its mitigation.

The buckets may not be per-caller at all. Both new endpoints key on HttpServletRequest.getRemoteAddr() and nothing sets server.forward-headers-strategy; behind the edge proxy this service is deployed behind, ANONYMOUS_CREATE's 30/min and SIGN_UP's 60/min are global ceilings, so one caller can deny sign-up and anonymous creation to everyone. docs/RUNBOOK.md:144 now documents the consequence but no code makes it configurable. This is a deployment fact the repository cannot show.

Unbounded concurrent Argon2id (16 MiB, ~25 ms each) is reachable unauthenticated on POST /api/v1/customers. The limiter fails open on any Redis RuntimeException, Tomcat's default max-threads is 200, and no thread cap or heap size is configured anywhere - worst case ~3.2 GiB transient allocation on the JVM that also serves redirects, during precisely the Redis outage when the click path leans hardest on it. Not covered by any test.

Connection-pool exhaustion by the same trigger, by a different mechanism: signUp() hashes inside the @Transactional boundary (eager acquisition assumed, not verified) and createAnonymous holds the transaction across a Redis round trip. Pool is the Hikari default of 10, shared with the redirect cache-miss fallback. Fixing either leaves the other.

V4's ALTER TABLE links takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE with no lock_timeout, during deploy, on the table the redirect path reads on every cache miss. It queues behind the longest in-flight query and every later query queues behind it, with Flyway blocking startup. One-line fix, not applied.

A documented 503 can surface as an undocumented 500: no fallback @ExceptionHandler, so a DataAccessException (pool exhaustion being the most likely producer) answers Boot's {timestamp,status,error,path} body, contradicting openapi.yaml's closed ApiError catalogue.
AC15's refusal half may never have executed - every 503 assertion in AnonymousCreateDegradationTest is conditional, so the service_unavailable envelope is unchecked if creation survives the outage.

Untested branches that would not fail anything if deleted: DenylistThreatCheck's fail-closed 'cannot canonicalise' path (TEST-2), HostNormalizer's IDN/punycode step (TEST-1), SignUpRequest's @Size(max=320) email boundary (TEST-4), and the accept side of host normalisation for ordinary public IP literals (TEST-3 - an implementation that over-refused every IP-literal target would pass all seventeen AC1/AC2 behaviours).

Test fragility: AnonymousLinkExpiryTest races a 3-second TTL with ~1.5s of margin on a loaded CI box (TEST-7), and AnonymousLinkCreationTest spends 25 of 30 anonymous-create tokens without pinning the limit (TEST-6), so adding two fixtures - which TEST-3 and SEC-9 both propose - breaks it as an unreadable status mismatch. The suite has also already failed once for harness capacity reasons (11 Spring contexts x pool of 10 against a 100-connection container), fixed by raising capacity, not by reducing contexts.

Accepted design positions that remain true after approval: the abuse-report takedown is immediate, unmoderated and irreversible with no unblock path and no owner recovery (updateExpiry answers 409 for a non-ACTIVE link), bounded now only by app.abuse.min-reporter-age=P7D - seven days of patience per cohort of minted accounts, not a removal of the attack; 409 account_unavailable remains an account-existence oracle (AC6 admits no non-disclosing wording); A4's 'no retroactive rescan' means every link already minted through the two bypasses this change closes keeps redirecting for up to 30 days while the service refuses to mint the same target.

Anonymous rows accumulate forever - unowned, undeletable, unreclaimed, each holding a (domain, code) slot and up to 2048 attacker-chosen bytes - with no purge job, no gauge and no alert. Growth rate is set by attacker choice.

Nobody reviewed adjacent surfaces this change makes more reachable: actuator endpoints sit outside the session filter and were assessed by no lens for what sign-up and anonymous-create volumes they now disclose; JWT issuance/verification was read at interface level only, and app.session.private-key-pem defaults to blank (ephemeral keypair per replica, untraced across replicas); clickCount exactness was not verified against the 'exact and current' promise.

AC3's failing-run evidence exists only because a human produced it by hand after the fact. The graph still has no node where new tests meet old code, so the next run has the same hole unless the missing node in docs/TODO.md is built.

Two pre-existing tracked defects (unvalidated {code} path variable with no fallback handler; CR/LF log injection through the same variable) were deliberately not re-reported and nobody confirmed they are still open.

orchestrator/sdlc/gates.py and orchestrator/tests/test_gates.py changed in this run's history (commit 7753468) and no lens audited that diff. A weakened gate would not have been visible from where any of the five lenses looked - and every mechanical outcome cited above is produced by that code.
